reason: The kernel implements the exact contract formulas (real=(a*c+b*d)/(c*c+d*d), imag=(b*c-a*d)/(c*c+d*d)) in fp32 with round-to-nearest division, returns a fresh fp32 [N,2] tensor, and preserves inputs. The only in-scope hypothesis (c1: fp32 intermediates cause tolerance violations on near-cancelling legal inputs) was rebutted by probe t7: on 100k worst-cancelled rows selected from 4M full-range random FP16 inputs (cancellation ratio down to 2.0e-7), max error/tolerance ratio was 0.298 with 0 violations and all outputs finite. Probe t10 covered remaining domain corners — extrema (±65504), subnormals, signed zeros, shared-backing-storage contiguous views — with 0 violations (max ratio 0.186, shared-view 0.243), all outputs finite, and inputs preserved. The math is sound: fp16×fp16 products are exact in fp32 (11+11-bit mantissas ≤ 24), so the fp32 RN sum error is relative to the (small) result, and div_rn adds at most one 2^-24 rounding, keeping total relative error well under the 5e-7 + 1e-7 tolerance for all legal FP16 inputs.
